Riley Fox laughed, coughed river, and lived. That night they found the first marker — an ancient carving that matched an ancient map exactly. The legend was real. It had always been real.

The river nearly ended it: rapids, a broken rope, Riley Fox in the water with an ancient map in a waterproof bag and the guide Kofi's hand the only solid thing in the world. 'Never leave a friend behind,' the guide Kofi gasped. 'Your rule.'

chapters.text:
the warlord's men's team hit them in the treasure chamber — of course it was the treasure chamber — and the standoff was pure cinema: an ancient map on its pedestal, two crews, one exit. 'Take it,' the warlord's men said, 'and die rich.'

Inside: wonders. the guide Kofi, the scholar at heart, wept at the murals. Riley Fox kept watch, because wonders in such places usually have teeth. They did: the floor was a trap, the walls were a trap, the air was a trap.

They emerged into daylight as the gate sealed forever behind the warlord's men's screams — no, wait. Riley Fox went back. Because curiosity is courage, and because no one gets left, not even the bad guys. They dragged the warlord's men out by the collar.
